*SHRI C. MAHENDRAN (POLLACHI): I express my hearty gratitude and indebtedness to our beloved immortal Leader Puratchi Thalavivi AMMA, before I place my views on the General Budget 2017-18.

Total Expenditure for 2018-19 estimated to be over Rs. 24.42 lakh crore. The total income expected is pegged at about Rs. 24 lakh crores. The total debts and other liabilities of the Government expected is about 90 Lakh Crores by the end of this financial year.

I would like to lay emphasis on the pressing needs of the people of the Kongu region of Tamil Nadu comprising my Pollachi Constituency. Coconut farming is an important occupation of people of Pollachi Parliamentary constituency. Coconut oil is the healthiest of edible oils. It is much healthier than Palmolein. There is a misconception that Coconut oil is high in cholesterol. There is a growing demand for supply of coconut and coconut oil through Public Distribution System. Instead of importing palmolein, indigenous production of coconuts has to be encouraged. By providing a good Minimum Support Price (MSP) for coconuts and to levy import dumping taxes for imported edible oils, indigenous production of coconuts will increase.

Tamil Nadu stands first in the production of coconuts (6917.25 Million Nuts) and productivity (14872 nuts/Ha). Tamil Nadu comes in third in terms of area cultivated under coconut. However the State faces challenges in maintaining the productivity of coconut groves due to severe pest and disease attacks and senile and unproductive palms. To increase yield, coconut palms have to be replanted.

Government of Tamil Nadu has proposed a special package with a total outlay a Rs. 3397.80 crores including subsidy of Rs. 757.95 crores to improve existing gardens, remove old/ senile palms and replant coconut seeding. The project covers 161 lakh palms in 92,000 hectares. As this scheme would raise yield and increase edible oil production the Government of India may kindly consider early sanction of scheme for the Rejuvenation and Replanting of Coconut Palms in Tamil Nadu. Farmers in my Pollachi Parliamentary Constituency depend mainly on a reasonable Minimum Support Price of Copra to ensure good income. But they are not getting the adequate support price for their Milling Copra and Ball Copra.

I have urged the Union Government to provide a support price of Rs. 140 per Kilogram for Milling Copra. But the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for "Milling Copra" has been fixed by the Cabinet Committee at Rs. 75 per kilo as per the recommendations by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP). This is inadequate at the time when Coconut farmers are already suffering a lot due to various factors like pest and insect problems, disease in coconut plants and poor yield.

The repeated requests of the Coconut farmers in the country for fixing the adequate MSP for Milling and Ball copra has left unaddressed by the Union Government. I urge upon the Union Government to fix the MSP at Rs. 140 per Kilo for the Milling and Ball Copra to enable them to earn a decent income and to come out from the clutches of the existing financial burden.

As far as Railways need of Kongu region, the expediting the completion of pending projects in Tamil Nadu must get the due attention of the Hon'ble Railway Minister. Sufficient funds may be allocated to increase the pace of ongoing railway projects in Tamil Naidu.

The gauge conversion work between Pollachi and Pothanur, Pollachi and Palakkad needs speedy completion. This will facilitate the restoration of all the trains which were in operation prior to the commencement of gauge conversion work.

Palani - Chennai Express Train, Palani - Tiruchendur Passenger Train and Palani - Madurai Passenger Train have been extended up to Pollachi. In order to overcome the rail traffic congestion from Coimbatore to Chennai, I would like to suggest and request the Hon'ble Minister for Railways to introduce two new express trains. This will benefit the people of Valparai, Pollachi, Palghat, Anamalai, Kinathukadavu, Udumalai, Madathukulam and also Palani.

These two new express trains may be introduced as Amma Express between Pollachi and Chennai Via. Dindigul and Trichy and as Anamalai Express between Pollachi and Bangaluru Via. Udumalai, Madathukulam, Palani, Dindigul, Karur, Salem, Dharmapuri and Hosur. This is necessary because the private and omni bus operator on these routes have fixed very high fares beyond the reach of the common people. The operation of these trains will greatly help the passengers while earning additional revenue for the railways.

The sections like Coimbatore - Pollachi - Udumalpet and other such sections that presently come under the Palaghat Division may kindly be transferred to Salem Division to enhance operational efficiency.

In order to overcome the problem of road traffic congestion in the areas under Coimbatore Corporation, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma took initiative to move away Ukkadam, Singanallur at Gandhipuram bus terminals. An integrated centralised bus stand to Vellalore at a cost of Rs. 300 crore is to come up. In order to integrate rail service facility also at this place Puratchi Thalaivi Amma, has taken up with the railways to establish a new railway station at Malumachampatti which is very nearer to Vellalore village. Since gauge conversion work is in progress in the Pollachi - Pothanur section of the railways, establishing a new railway station at Malumachampatti is immediately possible with the shifting of bus terminals from Coimbatore city and with the increase in the number of travelling public. Malumachampatti shall grow as an important country town.

The other important factor is that NH 147 and 209 and also State Highways No. 162 and 163 pass through Vellalore village. Vellalore and Malumachampatti are growing in size with many educational institutions and industrial units including MNC entities. A very big Truck Depot is to come up much near to Vellalore. Hence it is very much necessary to establish a new railway station at Malumachampatti with loading and unloading facility.

*SHRI T.G. VENKATESH BABU (CHENNAI NORTH):  At the outset, I would like to thank for giving me this opportunity to place my views on the Union Budget for 2018-19. 

This budget concentrates on areas hitherto neglected. For example, agriculture was neglected from 1991, when the nation as a whole plunged into the mantra of neo-liberalization and market reforms. There had been big ticket slogans on attracting FDI and ease of doing business, apart from boosting manufacturing and services sectors, relegating agriculture sector to the backburner. 

But after a long period, now the Central Government has realized, it seems, to focus on agricultural and allied growths. The Indian economy depends mainly on the agricultural sector which is the primary sector, without depending on which the manufacturing sector which is the secondary sector and the services sector which is the tertiary can sustain and grow. But successive governments were doing the opposite. Even this government was neglecting the agriculture sector to the effect that it could divert the workforce redundant in agriculture to other sectors. But the realization has dawned on this government at least at the fag-end of its rule. 

This budget is a model budget in sink with the TN Government's budget under the AIADMK rule enabled by our visionary, the great Amma, the former CM of TN, though it might have arrived with the ensuing election in mind. This budget is focused in uplifting the underprivileged, which constitute 60% of our population, mostly, living in rural areas, depending more on agriculture. 

The distress of farmers has been perennial because of low prices for their produce, suicides due to indebtedness, non-availability of irrigation and formal loan facilities. This budget has rightly focused on these areas of distress. This budget seems to have addressed the canons of taxing which spells that the strata of society who has the capacity to pay has to be taxed. 

The long pending demand of the farmers for a reasonable price for their produce is addressed in this budget, where almost all the 23 produces will get 1 ½   times of their cost of production as MSP (Minimum Support Price). As a result food subsidy is upped by a modest Rs.29,041 Cr. Apart from this the allocation of Rs.2000 Cr. for rural market fund and Rs.500 Cr. as Operation Green Fund to preserve perishables through increased warehousing facilities, doubling the allocation for food processing, easing restriction on exports of agricultural produce and products to reach their full potentiality of 100 billion dollars a year, crop credit to increase by 10% to Rs. 11 lakh crores. Lesser farmers will now have access to bank credit. Kisan Credit Cards to be given to Dairy and fisheries, the non-agriculture sector, by which the persons engaged in these sectors, will attain more credibility. The use of futures and options to forecast the demand and prices in the agricultural sector will enable farmers to bargain effectively. The creation of Gramin-Agri Markets, electronically linked e-NAM (National Agri. Market) and exempting them from APMC regulation are forward looking. The new MSP announced is to take off immediately covering the ensuing kharif season may be an initiative with an eye on elections. But these initiatives have come up because of the loud voices of the empowered farmers, who were hitherto voiceless. The farmers only aspire as to why elections can't be conducted every year, since every time a new Government takes over the centre, it neglects them for 3 years consecutively and at the end of the road in its last full budget takes care of the deprived including the farmers. But whatever may be reason behind, for the first time this budget addresses the problems of the farmers. This will boost agricultural production and ensure food security. 

The National Health Protection scheme may be the first big ticket and pioneering scheme in the world. But our Tamil Nadu Government has effectively implemented this scheme for many, many years benefitting lakhs of people. Much of the Insurance premium paid to the nationalized insurance company was diverted to government hospitals, strengthening the infra facilities in government hospitals, a clear shift from the previous DMK Government which engaged a private insurance company and siphoned off major funds to private hospitals. The NITI Aayog which is entrusted to work out the modalities for this scheme should turn a page from the Health Insurance scheme implemented in Tamil Nadu. Further, this is a centrally sponsored scheme devised by the centre for which the Centre takes the whole credit. But 40% of the expenditure has to be borne by the States under this scheme. How can a State like ours which has been effectively implementing this scheme share the expenditure? This is unfair and unjust. Further the fund allotted in this budget to this scheme is meager and grossly insufficient apart from the modalities not spelt out. There is an inherent danger in this scheme that instead of strengthening the primary and secondary health sectors, resources may be moved away to the tertiary health sector, where the private players will be benefitted enormously. 

The massive investment of Rs.14.34 lakh crore proposed for the development of rural infrastructure is another welcome scheme for road connectivity between urban and rural areas that will boost up employment potentialities in rural area. 

Free gas connection to 3 crore households, free electricity connection to 4 crore houses, 2 crore new toilets, higher micro-irrigation coverage will enable the poor to lead a decent life. But out of the net worth of Rs. 14.34 lakh crore to be allotted to this scheme, it is stated in the budget that 11.95 lakh crore is to be mobilized from the extra-budgetary resources. This casts a shadow on this project. 

The investment towards overall infra development is slated to be Rs.5.97 lakh crores, may boost up overall growth. But nearly Rs. 1 lakh crore of this investment is to be derived from the sale of public sector undertakings. The government is bound to lose one of its assets when newly acquiring another asset. This is a malady. 

This budget has billed around Rs. 1 lakh crore for 5 years. This will not suffice the growth of education. Our Amma's Government has spent nearly Rs. 1 lakh Cr. for education from 2011 to 2016 within the State. The Centre's allocation, when compared to ours pales into insignificance.

MSMEs (Medium, small and micro industry) is the worst hit due to demonetization and GST. Tamil Nadu tops the number of MSMEs in the whole of India. MSMEs contribute to nearly 90% of the employment potential. It is one area to which Amma gave utmost care and consideration. But due to demonetization nearly half of the industries vanished. The revival of them has become remote. The 5% Corporate Tax reduction offered to them in this budget Rs. 3 lakh crore loan to be extended to them under the mudra plan may not be sufficient to ease out. More care and help have to be extended to these industries, so that they come out of their problem and help in the nation building activity. Further raising the cap of sales from Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 250 crores is aimed at enabling a section of the big business also. Instead MSMEs are to be extended more facilities.

This budget, despite the buoyancy in the budgetary receipts expected is still relying more on extra budgetary resources and on external agencies. If they fail to deliver, that it will lead to a gap between promises and delivery.

This budget has belied the expectation of the salaried class who contribute about 90% of the direct taxes. The Rs. 40,000 relief given to them, without increasing the tax slab, will be offset by the increase in Education Cess by 1%. They have to pay Rs. 3000 crore additionally from their pockets.

There is nothing in this budget for Tamil Nadu. No fund has been allotted to be ongoing railway projects in the state. The Madurai-Kanyakumari and Tuticorin doubling project inaugurated by the Minister of State for Railways 10 days back is not funded. The 2nd phase of Metro and 4th terminal of Tondiarpet proposed by the Southern Railway Administration were also neglected. 

During the year the Government has made a highest ever allocation of Rs. 1.48 lakh crore to the Railways and there was also mention about strengthening of Mumbai and Bangalore Railway network. During 2018-19, Tamil Nadu has been allotted a mere Rs. 2,548 crore for the ongoing doubling, electrification, new lines, gauge conversion and other development works of railways. The major omission is the long pending demand of converting the Tondiarpet Railway Station into Chennai's fourth 

railway terminal. Earlier Railways proposed to convert the historic Royapuram railway station into a terminal but this project found to be not feasible due to space constraints and geographical restrictions. Now the Southern Railway plan to convert Tondiarpet railway station, 7 km. north of Chennai Central into fourth railway terminal as there is ample land on the western and eastern side of the existing station. It will drastically ease the congestion and burden on the Chennai Central and Egmore stations. I urge upon the Union Government to expedite the proposal to allocate adequate funds during this fiscal year.

The construction of AIIMS hospitals proposed and sanctioned to Tamil Nadu has also not been funded. The Centre is to start new hospitals over India at the rate of one in 2 MP constituencies. In Tamil Nadu, we have already got one hospital in each district. Many of them are upgraded as Medical College hospitals. None of the schemes in TN, viz. the Athikadavu-Avinashi Water project to which the Center has given approval has been allotted with funds. TN has got the largest GST data base and pay a lot of tax to the centre but it is neglected in the centraly and State sponsored schemes.

The river linking was once a pet programme of BJP. But not a single project was taken up by BJP in the last 4 years of its rule. Tamil Nadu's persistent demand for linking peninsular rivers and for linking intra-state rivers did not find favour with the Centre. The Centre could allot funds for Mumbai and Bangalore suburban but is grossly neglecting the Chennai suburban rail traffic.

How the resource crunch affects the ambitious projects of this Government can be understood in the establishment of 99 Smart Cities, out of which one percent only is completed, 10% is going on and the remaining are yet to take off. No Smart City project in TN is funded so far. This malady extends to other projects also despite the buoyancy in tax collection.

The performance of this Government in generating employment opportunities is dismal. Out of the promise of generating 2 crore jobs every year, they could not reach that one year target even after more than 3 years of rule.

Every Government has to choose between populism and fiscal prudence. This Government is averse to violate the FRBM Act to limit its fiscal deficit within 3% of GDP, but has failed marginally. But to abide by the fiscal consolidation policy, it has to forgo public expenditure and social welfare schemes, which are essential to boost up the economy, when the private operators are hesitant to invest.

This Government has to be still credited that it exercises several options to stem the tide and is constantly experimenting but fails miserably. Take for example, the newly introduced 10% Capital Gain Tax on the equity shares of Rs. 1 lakh held for more than one year but has to grandfather it by fixing the period upto 31st January 2018 as non-taxable. Still there were some turmoil in the stock market initially but arrested due to grandfathering. 

Likewise, the Government is dithering as to whether to increase the import duty or to reduce it. In the last budget, it reduced the import duty for reasons prescribed, but this year it has increased the duty on reasons specified. The government has reasons for both.

"Growth is never by choice, it is the result of forces working together" is the famous quote in economy. In UPA, the growth was by choice but in NDA it is optional.

With these words, I conclude my speech.

*SHRI S.P. MUDDAHANUME GOWDA (TUMKUR): The Budget presently by the Hon. Finance Minister, Shri Arun Jaitley, for the year 2018-19 is, to some extent, disappointing. Lot of Members of Parliament have partcipated in the discussion and have stated many factors with regard to the General Budget 2018-19. Few Members have welcomed the Budget and majority of the Opposition Members who spoke from the Opposition side have opposed the Budget. I oppose the Budget for the following few reasons.

The Budget does not address any concern of the country. That is why, we find here that manufacturing sector is not growing up. Unemployment is just knocking our doors afflicting the economy, society and the country. The Public sector investment is coming down and not taking up. Private investment is just coming down in the last three years. The need of the hour is to accelerate the economy and to promote the consumption but this Budget does not have anything substantial on this. 

This Budget is not providing any immediate relief to farmers. Farmers are committing suicide as they are debt-ridden. The facility of crop insurance is given to only those farmers who have taken loans from banks. That means in the event of any natural calamity, the banks will get benefitted from the crop insurance. Farmers should be given 100 per cent subsidy for micro irrigation. The subsidy meant for farmers should directly be given to the farmers not to the companies. Similarly, the benefit of crop insurance should directly go the farmers. Farm loans of all the farmers should be waived off.

The Budget even does not mention minimum support price to farmers which is absolutely essential. There is meager increase in the budgetary allocation for MGNREGA. There is no increase or less increase in allocation for PMGSY and Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana and Smart Cities Programme.

The Hon. Finance Minister has not made anything about the underprivileged, dalit, minority and poor classes of the people.

The Budget allocation for Railways is not upto the expected lines. For this, the hon. Railway Minister could not even protest and he should have asked for more Budget from the Hon. Finance Minister. Due to the very meager allocation to the Railways, the Railway safety will, most probably, be compromised.

Hon. Finance Minister has failed to announce any relief to the middle-class and salaried class people. The announcement of Standard Deduction of Rs.40,000/- and removing Transport Allowance and Medical Allowance, which comes to Rs.34,200/- from the income tax relief is an just eye-wash announcement of the Hon. Finance Minister, without changing tax slabs. The announcement of the Finance Minister, instead of giving happiness to the salaried and middle class people, irritated them a lot. The people, especially salaried middle class people, expected more from the Hon. Finance Minister on the individual tax rates. But, they are very much disappointed with the announcement of the Hon. Finance Minister. I urge upon the Finance Minister to keep the tax rate of 5 per cent, 15 per cent and 25 per cent as against the present 5 per cent, 20 per cent and 30 per cent, which will help the middle class people on their tax liability. 

Allocation for schemes relating to rural roads, rural drinking water, education, mid-day meal programme and urban development are stagnant. Initiatives related to job creation for the youth is an area of serious concern where adequate focus is not given. 

Lastly, I request the hon. Finance Minister to increase the MPLADS funds to Rs.15 crore so that the Members of Parliament can take up more developmental activities/ works in their Constituencies and to help the people.

Thank you.

*SHRI R. DHRUVANARAYANA (CHAMARAJANAGAR): I would like to convey my sincere thanks for providing an opportunity to place my views and concerns on Union Budget 2018. The union budget 2018 addresses packages of ambitions, dreams and many more new promises in Rural development, Education, Health Care, Agriculture sectors. But, it's just a bubble on water. 

I would like to call this budget yet another budget of false promises and unfaithful commitments on development, employment. Government is lack of long term result-oriented goals for the welfare of this nation. 

During 2014 general election campaign both Hon'ble Prime Minister of India and Hon'ble Finance Minister of India of current union government, have promised Indian citizens on increasing the personal tax exemption limit to Rs. 5 lakh. Even after four years in ruling and even after four budgets. Union government was unable to fulfill the promise made for citizens of this great nation. This is one of example on record how government is lacking in delivering its own promises. 

Every year Government is coming up with new schemes and programs in the name of development and promise of change. But in real time, Government is becoming utterly failed in meeting the goals, which has set for itself. As an evidence Swatch Bharat initiative. If you look at the figures, the current year budget allocation for this program has gotten reduction of 7.3% (Rs. 1,405 crores less) budgetary allocation. This is one simple example on how Union Government is misleading the citizens of this nation. 

This year Union Government has come with a new program of Health Insurance for poor people. But what is bothering us is budget needed to implement this program into reality. Target to provide promised health cover for 80 crores poor people up to Rs. 5 1akhs. Total cost is going to be incurred for successful implementation of this program is Rs. 12,000 crores. Government doesn't have a clear vision on how required money will be generated. 

Government has made an announcement on increase of MSP by 1.5 times for agriculture crops. The fact is government has not reserved/allocated the sufficient required fund for effective implementation of program. It is yet another example of lack of vision on farmers welfare. 

Since 2014, Hon'ble Prime Minister is keep saying about distressed farmers that the income of farmers will be doubled by 2022. Even after four budgets, there is no clarity on how union government is going to achieve this goal. Not even a single program which is aimed to facilitate the farmers to gain revenue till date. 

Government is doing nothing for the welfare of vulnerable, depressed class people welfare. Government does not have visionary views, plans for upliftment of these societies. As an evidence government has reduced the budgetary allocation for welfare of Schedule Caste and Schedule Tribes. As per the population ratio, government supposed to be made an allocation of Rs. 1,43,415 crores for Schedules Caste component program as per the population but it has allotted only Rs. 56,690 crores, which is nearly 40% reduction. Similarly, for Schedule Tribes component it has allotted only Rs. 39,135 crores instead of Rs. 74,299 crores. 

Herewith I strongly appeal the Union Government to make the corrections of budgetary allocation for welfare of Schedule Caste and Tribes as per the population ratio. 

The most affected class in the society due to the adverse actions of Union Government are common man, middle class salaried people. The increase in cess (Education + health) from 3 to 4% will not only impact the in-hand salaries but also adversely impact the economy and will escalate the inflation rates. As on date the common man/salaried people paying four different taxes on their hard earned money i.e. GST, Long Term Capital gain Tax, Income Tax and Increased Cess on Income tax. But it had promised them Acche Din. 

The Government who came to power with a promise of Acche Din, Change and Development, even after four years in power except burden of new taxes, surcharges, cess, people got nothing in return for their welfare. 

Union Government has promised for shelter or house for every poor people of this nation. But in adverse the budgetary allocation for Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) has got the reduction of 5.3% (Rs. 1,538 crores less). This is yet another evidence of how difference in his speech and actions in delivering his promises and in welfare of common man. 

Government made promise to concentrate on welfare of Rural India. In contradiction, its budgetary allocation for Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana which is aimed at strengthening the rural agriculture and rural electrification has got reduction of 29.63% (Rs. 1,600 crores). These facts reveal how much Union Government is incompetent. 

Government is not committed for the welfare of the nation and its people, but it works to facilitate few corporate families. The common man, farmer, middle class salaried people are in great distress, protesting in streets. Small scale businessmen have closed their business. Middle class salaried people are fighting to save their honest earnings, struggling to save their earnings against increased inflation, unable to provide good education and required health facilities for their dear once. The rate of farmers' suicide has kept increasing year by year. 

The Government has no vision on protecting the farmers and their dependents, agriculture production. Agriculture sector is facing a greater threat due to climate change. Government has done nothing to establish early warning system of monsoon rainfall to avoid crop loss. 

I would like to make kind appeal to the government to come up with more growth oriented, inclusive budget for the welfare of all sections of the society. Make a special attention towards agriculture sector, welfare of depressed class people. 

*श्री राजकुमार सैनी (कुरूक्षेत्र): बजट भाषण में आपने मुझे शामिल होने का मौका दिया इसके लिए धन्यवाद। हमारे वित्त मंत्री जी ने बजट में रेलवे के लिए एक बहुत बड़े अंशदान का प्रावधान किया है जिसमें रेलवे की नई लाइनें बिछाने का भी कार्यक्रम है। मैं कुरूक्षेत्र लोक सभा से आता हूं, जिसको पर्यटन के तौर पर बढ़ावा देने के लिए माननीय प्रधानमंत्री द्वारा विभिन्न स्कीमों में विशेष तर्जी देने का प्रावधान है। इस क्षेत्र में पर्यटक, देश भर से आते हैं इसलिए यहां पर पटियाला पंजाब से गुहला पेहवा कुरूक्षेत्र लाडवा यमुनानगर को नई रेलवे लाइन बिछाने की बहुत पुरानी मांग है। अभी हाल ही में एक ट्रेन हरिद्वार के लिए कैथल होते हुए कुरूक्षेत्र अंबाला छावनी होते हुए चलाई गई है जो कि यह सीधा रूट नहीं बनता जिससे यात्रियों को असुविधा होती है इसलिए पटियाला से गुहला पेहवा कुरूक्षेत्र लाडवा यमुनानगर तक यह लाइन बिछाई जाएं ताकि कुरूक्षेत्र धर्मनगरी व हरिद्वार धर्मनगरी का सीधा संपर्क हो सके और पर्यटन को बढ़ावा मिले। 

मुझे बजट पर अपने विचार रखने का मौका दिया गया, माननीय वित्त मंत्री जी ने किसानों की आर्थिक दशा सुधारने के लिए बजट में काफी प्रावधान किया है। जिसमें किसान की आय दोगुनी करने के लिए अनेक प्रयासों का उल्लेख है । किसान व मजदूर सिक्के के दो पहलू हैं । मजदूरों को मनरेगा स्कीम के माध्यम से जो पैसा दिया जाता है उसमें बहुत बड़ा भाग भ्रष्टाचार की भेंट चढ़ जाता है। जो देश के विकास में काम नहीं आता । देश के विकास में जो परम्परागत ढांचा है उसका निर्माण तो टेंडर सिस्टम से होता है लेकिन इन मजदूरों के पास किसी प्रकार का कोई काम नहीं है । फर्जी मेस्ट्रोलो के द्वारा पैसा निकाल लिया जाता है । इन मजदूरों को किसानों के साथ जोड़ दिया जाए जितना पैसा मनरेगा स्कीम से दिया जाता है उतना ही पैसा किसान भी मजदूरों को देगा जिससे मजदूर की आमदनी दोगुनी हो जाएगी और किसान को आधे रेट में मजदूर मिल जाएगा । इससे उसकी मजदूरी खर्चे में सहायता मिलने से खेती सस्ती हो जाएगी । आमदनी दोगुना हो जाएगी, देश की जनता जब व्यवहारिक रूप में काम करने लगेगी किसान व मजदूर दोनों मालामाल हो जाएंगे व अर्थव्यवस्था को मजबूती मिलेगी ।

*SHRI G. HARI (ARAKKONAM): I express my hearty gratitude and indebtedness to our beloved immortal Leader Puratchi Thalaivi AMMA, before I place my view on the General Budget 2017-18.

The new India Budget aims at an enhanced ease of Living. The Ayushman Bharat is envisaged to give health insurance cover of Rs.5 lakhs to around 10 crore families is laudable. But I would like to record here that similar health insurance scheme for poor households is already implemented by the Government of Tamil Nadu.

1.5 Wellness Centres to provide improved healthcare for people in rural villages, 2 crore toilets to be constructed under Swachh Bharat is the need of the hour. But I wish to emphasize that adequate supply of water is very crucial and it is the duty of the Union Government to provide a financial component for adequate water supply for the better maintenance of toilets. Otherwise instead of providing hygience and good health the very same can become a haven for diseases through unclean toilets.

The target for Ujwalla Yojana raised to 8 crore beneficiaries in this Budget. I urge upon the Government to maintain an equiTable share on the population of the States in the country otherwise the better performing states will have lesser number of beneficiaries.

This budget aims to create a New India where agriculture and farmers welfare is given top priority and lion's share. A record allocation of Rs.14.34 lakh crore for Rural Development and Agriculture and providing one and half times of their production cost as MSP to Farmers are very significant. But here too the State-wise allocation of the funds for Rural Development and Agriculture need to be equiTable to both population and number of rural villages. The creation of 22,000 Gramin Agriculture Markets to help farmers to sell their produce directly is praiseworthy. The target for Public Sector Banks to provide loans for farmers is raised to Rs.11 lakh crores. This is really welcome. But here too the Government and Banks should benefit genuine needy farmers. There should not be any denial or delay in disbursement of loans to deserving poor farmers irrespecitve of their land holdings and in fact priority should be accorded to micro, small and marginal farmers instead of big landlords having vast empire of landholdings. 

I would like to bring to the notice of the Government the important long pending demands of the People of my Arakkonam Constituency with regards to Railway. The Tindivanam - Nagari New line has been sanction long back, but due to the non allocation of sufficient funds it has remained incomplete for a long period. I would urge upon the Government to take necessary action to benefit lakhs of the people from my Arakkonam Constituency.

The Arakkonam and Katpadi are very important Railway Junctions in Southern Railway. These two Railway Junctions need Modernization with all facilities with state of art technology. There is an urgent need for Railway Over Bridge at Katpadi and requires immediate sanction and execution.

The Marudalam and Itchiputhur Railway stations need to be upgraded. Platforms need to be extended and provided with all amenities. All trains have to be stopped at these two stations. The Shilinghur, Banavaram and Tiruttani EMUs need more frequency as large number of rail passengers are using this sectors. 

I would like to bring to the notice of the Government about an important and long pending demand of people of my Arakkonam Constituency for extending the Arakkonam -Velachery EMU fast rain (Train No. 43936) up to Tiruttani Station.

Due to insufficient frequency of EMU Train in the Morning hours between 7.00 am to 8.50 am, most of the train commuters are facing huge hardship travelling to and from Chennai. There is an urgent need for extending the said train up to Tiruttani for the benefit of train passengers in this area.

If the above said train starts from Tiruttani instead of Arakkonam it will be beneficial for many train passengers living in and around Arakkonam Parliamentary Constituency.

The Trivandrum Mail Train No. 12624 towards Chennai crossing the Arakkonam Junction at 5.45 am does not stop at Arakkonam but stops at Avadi only. Since the train has not having a stoppage at Arakkonam the passengers who want to get down at Arakkonam have to travel upto Avadi and catch a train to come back to Arakkonam. This is unnecessary and lot of passengers, particularly elderly people and women with children are suffering a lot because of this.

To avoid the inconvenience I request the Hon. Minister to direct the concerned authorities in Southern Railway to provide stoppage for the Train No.12624 - Trivandrum Mail at Arakkonam Junction. 

*SHRI LADU KISHORE SWAIN (ASKA): It is high time to remember that this government was elected with the mandate in reducing corruption, gaining employment opportunities to youth and women, and reducing the gap of rich and poor while ensuring and sustaining higher economic growth. Union Budget 2018-19 is the fifth and the final full-year budget of the incumbent government. In this regard, it was expected a number of progressive welfare measures that would be announced by the Finance Minister in his budget speech 2018-19 with adequate budget support. Like business as usual, current budget again betrayed all the hopes of millions, including the expectations of the farmers, corporate giants, youths and particularly the marginalised sections of the society. 

The focus of the Union Budget 2018-19 missed the golden opportunity of gaining the confidence of the rural community, especially the farmers' and youths. The current budget has several heatless announcements for agriculture and rural infrastructure development, generating employment opportunities in the formal sector, providing quality healthcare for underprivileged and senior citizens and improving the provisions for education. The emphasis on generating productive and gainful on-farm and non-farm employment for the farmers and landless families has not adequately been backed by the union budget allocations for the year 2018-19. 

The Union Budget 2018-19 could have been clearly marked with higher budget allocations for education, health, social welfare measures for women, children, SCs and STs. However, the Union Budget 2018-19 only offers lofty of promises for the farmers in this country without having a clear roadmap of strategies in doubling the farmers' income by 2022. This budget not only disappointed, but also showed the high degree of arrogance that this government has by not taking care of the pledges of the millions. 

The presentation of the Union Budget 2018-19 on the floor of Parliament by the Finance Minister again lost the confidence of the millions by not prioritizing allocations that was expected for the sectors like rural employment, agriculture, rural connectivity and for creating employment opportunities for the youths, including rural housing programme. The MGNREGA allocations maintain a status quo at 55,000 crores. The emphasis on MSMEs to generate entrepreneurship opportunities and create employment in the economy has not been adequately budgeted for Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, hailed as a success as more than 10 crore beneficiaries last year, indicates employment challenges have been tackled through creation of self-employment programmes rather than wage employment programmes. The target for skill development for 50 lakh youth in 2018-19 through skill India without adequate budget support would remain as promises of this government. 

Government announced 'Housing for All' and a target for 1 crore houses to be built by March 2019, with 51 lakh in FY 2018 and 51 lakh in FY 2019. As per Government's achievement report, only 12.6 lakh houses have been constructed, which is only 12.6% of the total target of 1 crore households. Moreover, budgetary allocation to Pradhan Mantri Aawas Yojana Grameen decreased by 9% in the current budget from the previous year. 

The allocation for National Social Assistance Programme to the tune of Rs. 420 crores in 2018-19 (BE) as compared to 2017-18 BE. The main focus here has been the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension scheme. The allocation for Rashtriya Swastha Bima Yojana has increased to Rs. 2000 crore and it promises the health care for millions through the insurance model without focusing on improving the health care institutions and addressing the concern of human resource shortages. The announcement of National Health Protection Scheme for 10 crore poor and vulnerable families (50 crore beneficiaries) is not backed by any budgetary allocation. 

The budget for education has increased from Rs.79686 Crore in 2017-18 (BE) to Rs.85010 Crore in 2018-19(BE); a 6.7 percent increase; however the share of education budget in Union budget has decreased from 3.7 percent in 2017-18(BE) to 3.5 percent in 2018-19 (BE). This shows the Government's commitments towards improving the standard and quality education in the country. 

The Government has still not come up with a revised framework for earmarking under Scheduled Caste Sub Plan, which dilutes the implementation of the strategy. Budget allocation for Post Matric scholarship for Scheduled Castes has declined from Rs. 3,348 crore in 2017-18 (RE) to Rs. 3,000 crore in 2018-19 (BE). This reduced allocation comes at a time when the department has been asking for a one-time package to clear the accumulated arrears under the same amounting to Rs. 8,000 crore at the end of 2016-17. No revised framework for earmarking under Tribal Sub Plan (TSP) has been formulated and ministries continue to report under TSP from scheme allocations. This fails to ensure need-based planning and budgeting for the Scheduled Tribes and what gets reported in TSP is a largely incidental benefit accruing from general schemes. 

To promote best quality education to the tribal children in their own environment Government of India has decided that by the year 2022, every block with more than 50% ST population and at least 20,000 tribal persons, will have an Ekalavya Model Residential School. The allocation for this year is Rs.1800 crore, an increase from Rs. 1500 crore in 2017-18(BE), is a welcome step. Allocations for Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana, Swadhar Grih and National Créche Scheme have witnessed a decline in 2018-19 (BE) in comparison to 2017-18 (BE). Poor progress is witnessed on ensuring that legislative frameworks for anti-corruption, grievance redress and whistle-blower protection. There has been great focus on positioning Aadhar and DBT as a means of reducing corruption thereby enhancing savings of the public exchequer. However, the verdict is contested as the methodology of computing savings earned due to Aadhar based DBT in social sector schemes has not been shared. Currently, no Ministry is allocating dedicated funds for investing in processes that enhance public accountability. It is therefore recommended to provide 0.5 % of budget to institutionalize mechanisms for transparency, grievance redress and citizen accountability across development schemes. 

*SHRI ANTO ANTONY (PATHANAMTHITTA): First of all, I would like to express my profound sorrow over the Union Budget 2018 as it failed to overhaul the damages incurred to the national economy due to the economic mismanagement of the NDA Government. This Government has caused irreparable damages to the economy in a short span of time.

A comparison of two Economic Surveys released by the present NDA Government will tell what has happened to our economy during the last four years. The Economic Survey of 2014-15 presented by this NDA Government stated that the economy was performing well during that time as its fundamentals were very strong. But the recent Economic Survey states that the economy has been weakened. It does not require much knowledge in economics to reach a conclusion that the economic mismanagement of the present NDA Government and its anti-poor policies have pushed our economy into this dangerous situation.

Father of our great Nation, Mahatma Gandhi rightly opined that " India lives in villages". The valuable advice he had given to the future statesmen was to frame pro-poor policies so that the poorest of the poor in the country could be empowered. It should be noted that the Instruction bequeathed by the Mahatma has been well considered by the First Central Government to the previous UPA-II Government. Through various programmes and policies ranging from the Five Year Plan to the bank Nationalization and the recent Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS), these governments were building a new nation brick-by-brick from a colony looted by the British. These governments led by the Congress Party, kept well the advice of Mahatma Gandhi that India lives in villages and agriculture is its backbone. These governments were keen to bolster agriculture sector and rural economy through novel experiments such as Green Revolution, Bank Nationalization etc. The thriving economy at the grass-roots level, especially in the agriculture and rural sector, helped to maintain a high growth rate when the global economy was undergoing a recession.

The positive impacts of the UPA-II Government on economy have continued even during the first two years of the present NDA Government. The recent Economic Survey released by this Government also acknowledges this truth that the Indian economy was strong till 2016. The only thing this Government had to take care of was to keep the pace of the economic growth. Instead of doing that the present Government has been trying to destroy the economy ever since it assumed the power in 2014. The present crisis is the result of the economic mismanagement and foolishness on the part of the Government. Among them the decision to demonetize high-value currencies and the poor implementation of GST has wreaked havoc on the lives of farmers, small traders and people depend on small scale-cottage industries and informal sector for their livelihood.

The Budget 2018 was the last opportunity for the present Government to revive Indian economy, however, the Government miserably failed in this mission. The Budget Speech of the Hon'ble Finance Minister was the repetition of the hollow promises made by the Government. Moreover, Hon'ble Minister has declared certain ambitious schemes. However, the meager outlays to these ambitious schemes reveal that the Government is aimed at only making publicity. For instance, the Government claims that the income of farmers will be doubled by 2022. The committee constituted by the Government to set forth recommendations for doubling farmers' income estimated that an amount of Rs. 63990000 lakh crore was required for achieving this ambitious target. However, the Government has nothing done to fulfill this promise, as only four years left to 2022. For instance, Total outlay for agriculture during the Financial Year 2018-19 is only Rs. 42211 crore. Out of this, the outlay for the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna is Rs. 13000 crore, and Interest Subsidy for short term credit to farmers is Rs. 15000 crore. The outlay for the irrigation project, named as Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojna is Rs. 4000 crore. Target of the allocation for the mechanization of agriculture during 2018-19 is Rs.1100 crore. Hon'ble Minister also declared an outlay of Rs. 3100 crore for the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana. This Scheme is for the development of infrastructure such as cold storages, godowns and labs etc. and the amount in this regard is only Rs. 3100 crore. These are the outlay for 2018-19 for advancing the Government's mission- the doubling of farmers' income by 2022.

Hon'ble Minister in his Budget Speech reiterated the Government's commitment to ensure farmers a return of one- and -a- half times of the cost of their production. However, the fund is not earmarked for the procurement of crops at this enhanced rate. Then how can the Government ensure a return that is one-and-a-half times of the cost of production. Not only that, the Food Corporation of India is gradually withdrawing from the procurement of food grains as per the new policy of the Government. Then how can the Government ensure that the farmers are getting reasonable prices for their produces? 

Hon'ble Finance Minister has declared on outlay of Rs. 13000 crore for the Pradhan Mantri Fasal BIma Yojna during 2018-19. The Scheme is claimed to ensure crop insurance for the farmers in the country. However, the reality is that this Scheme helps only the insurance companies as they have already collected a large amount of premium from the Government and poor farmers. However, only 20 percent of the farmers got the benefits of this Scheme and about 80 percent of claims were rejected. According to reports, the private insurance companies amassed an unlawful dividend of Rs. 994 crore from this Scheme last year alone.

Irrigation projects are vital for the agriculture sector of the country. At present, the irrigation projects in the agriculture sector are implemented under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojna and the Government has declared an outlay of Rs. 4000 crore for the Financial Year 2018-19. The amount is meager compared with the requirement. Lack of the fund is one of the reasons for the delayed irrigation projects. It should be noted that only four out of 23 large irrigation projects in the country will be fully operational by March 2018. The delay in this regard is actually affecting the growth of agriculture sector in the country.

The Government is repeating the hollow promise of 'doubling income' at a time the nation witnesses the growing tide of farmers' protests. The Government failed to arrest declining income of farmers, and prevent the farmer suicides. The Government also failed to convince not only the farmers, but also its allies, supporters and even its elected representatives. Recently, one Member of Parliament, who got elected to the Lok Sabha on the BJP ticket, resigned due to the anti-farmer policies of the Government. Instead of correcting its erring policies the Government is cracking down on the farmers' protest with its coercive apparatus.

If we compare the outlay for rural infrastructure with the growing pace of inflation, we will realize that this sector is gaining nothing. The outlay for the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) is Rs. 19000 crore. This amount is to realize 57,000 km of rural roads and 28.35 crore mandays.

Like that of agriculture Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are also playing a major role in generating employment. Demonetization and GST have already affected MSMEs. However, the outlay for reviving MSMEs is a meager Rs. 2908 crore.

Spiral hikes in the prices of petroleum products and food items contributing to the inflation in the country, which may cross 5.2 per cent. However, the Budget Speech kept silence on the inflation and steps to arrest it. In order to control inflation the then UPA Government provided subsidy for petroleum products at a time the price of crude oil was high. It should be noted that the price of crude oil per barrel was $ 100 in January 2014. However, the price of the crude oil, halved by the end of November 2014, and it remains at the lowest ebb in recent history. However, the Government is not ready to bring its benefits to the common people in the country. As a result, inflation has also marked an all time high rate. If the Government could reduce the duty on petroleum products, inflation in the country could be arrested to a great extent. It is learnt that the Government has already collected an amount of Rs. 1.6 lakh crore as a duty.

The rate of fiscal deficit is also alarming in the country. The Government has opted for wider fiscal deficit at 3.5 per cent of GDP for the year 2018-19. Higher rate of fiscal deficit will adversely affect foreign investment in the country. The Government may also take note of the declining foreign investment in the country. Declining investment will definitely affect employments, production and, naturally, the economic growth. A responsible Government will enhance the public investment to offset the shortage of private and foreign investment. However, what is alarming is the Government's reluctance to take up its responsibility in this regard.

Even though the youth in the country is badly in need of skill training, the Government's outlay for the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) is only Rs. 1171 crore. Not only that the number of beneficiaries curtailed down drastically to 18. This also shows the Government's lack of determination to create the promised rate of two crore employments per annum.

While the Government claims that it is dedicated to empower women, its allocation in this regard is minimal. For instance, the Government has curtailed outlay for the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana from Rs. 2700 crore in 2017-18 to Rs. 2400 crore in 2018-19. Even though, atrocities against the women is on the rise, the outlay for the Nirbhaya Fund Schemes is Rs. 500 crore and there is no increase from last year. In the same manner a meager increase is marked in the outlay for the Child Protection Scheme in 2018-19, Rs.725 crore compared with Rs. 648 crore in 2017-18.

The Budget ignored the welfare of the persons with disabilities as various Schemes for the employment of Persons with Disability. Last year it was Rs. 855 crore and increased to Rs. 1070 crore in 2018-19. It should be noted that the Government has stopped funding for the insurance scheme for the disabled due to the acute financial crunch. In the same manner, the Government also ignored the welfare of the senior citizens, as the allocation for the National Social Assistance Programme is also very poor.

The plight of the Anganwadi workers may continue without much change as the outlay is only Rs. 16335 crore in 2018-19. The outlay for Higher Education is also a meager amount of Rs. 35010 crore, and still the Government claims that is will erect world class institutions of higher education and research in the country.

Since school education in the country is vexing with the problem of whopping number of dropout, outlay is not enough to address this issue. The amount is located in this regard is Rs. 50000 crore, and out of this Rs. 26129 crore is for Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and Rs. 4022 crore is for Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan. Outlay to the mid-day meal scheme is also meagerly increased from Rs. 10000 crore in 2017-18 to Rs. 10500 crore in 2018-19.

Even though the claims over the Schemes such as the Make in India, the Start-Up India, Digital India, Skill India Programme, Stand Up India, etc. are very high, the outlays to these schemes are comparatively minimal. The Government launched the Mudra Scheme with much fanfare and publicity, the average amount of Mudra loan is Rs. 43000.

The middle class starting from the annual income of Rs. 25000 expected a revision in the income tax. However, the Budget brought them disappointment. If the Government could provide the tax relief to them, then it could stir the demand in consumer goods. That could have stimulated the markets, but due to the reluctance on the part of the Government that did not happen. 

They ignored the public health sector as the allocation for Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana is increased by Rs. 672 crore. The reality is that it will take a minimum of Rs. 60,000 crore for the implementation of this Scheme. Despite the meager allocation for Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana, the Government is promising a National Health Protection Scheme which will cover 10 crore poor and vulnerable families. The coverage will be upto Rs. 5 lakh. Having considered the hollow promises of the Government this should be considered as another ambitious Scheme never to be fulfilled.

The Budget also neglected the Defence Sector, at a time the national security is under threat by the moves of our neighbouring countries. This Sector witnessed a meager increase of 7.8 per cent and not in touch with the current realities. The allocation to Defence is less than 1.8 percent of the GDP. Number of security personnel losing their lives in fight against terrorists and cross-border firings are also increasing in the country. We have to ensure the safety of our security personnel, who are protecting our nation from domestic and external threats. However, the Budget also ignored the plight of our defence personnel.

In short, the Budget could bring only disappointment as it ignored and neglected the key sectors of economic growth, human resource development, social security, and also requirements for domestic and external security.

As can be seen, most of the serious issues promised in the Election Manifesto of the BJP during the last Election have not been addressed during last 4 years. For some, the Government has come up with proposals now, in the last budget. Had these issues been taken up from day one of taking over the charge, many of these problems could have been addressed. All these new schemes and proposals cannot be met within a year.

It does not seen to be a one year budget speech. The budget seems to be a Five Year Plan. The tenure of the government is coming to an end within a year. Hence talking 2022 or beyond has no relevance at this point of time. It seems the Government has brought these schemes now to allure the voters, keeping the ensuing General Election in mind.

It is crediTable that one Dalit has been elected as the President of India. But, with this only justice to the Dalits and weaker section of the society has not been addressed. The promise of still working towards strengthening social justice and economic democracy to usher ease of living for the common man is far from reality. Many cases of atrocities towards Dalits and weaker section, beating them , lynching them, denying them entry to places of worship, denying them common facilities like drinking water are still reported from across the country.

Banks are denying loans to the Tribals on the plea that their land is not mortgagable. Their children are denied education loans. They cannot afford education in Private Educational Institutes as they cannot afford the exorbitant fees charged by the Private Institutes.

Quality private institutions have been the privilege of a few. This has created a situation of "Reverse & Reservation to the Rich". Talking of establishing Ekalavya Schools in each Tribal Block is too little and too late. There is no regular cadre of teachers in existing schools. The Government's claim of making these schools at par with Navodaya Vidyalas is only an illusion.

The promise of BJP in their election manifesto about equality and equal opportunities is far from the reality. BJP's promise to establish "National Centre for Tribal Research" has not been addressed.

The demand by various corners for fund allotment proportionate to the population of SC, ST & Other weaker sections has not been addressed. The authors of the Constitution kept certain provisions, including reservation in Government services, with the hope that after some period they will be at par with rest of the people in all fields i.e., socially, economically, educationally and culturally. No visible progress is seen in these fields. They continue to be vote bank for some party of or other with the hope that some party will do justice to them.

Many proposals for inclusions of deserving castes into the Scheduled List of SC, ST and Backward classes are pending with the Government even after 70 years of Independence. 

As against requirement of about 13 lakh Doctors, only about 8 lakh registered Doctors are in practice. There is a gap of about 5 lakh Doctors. Opening only 24 New Medical Colleges is not going to the fill the gap. There is large shortage of para-medical staff which has not been addressed. Facilities in the Government Hospitals are far from adequate.

Most of the issues promised in the Manifesto of BJP have not been addressed on health sector. 

New Health Insurance Policy is not going to address the real issue. When there is shortage of infrastructure and skilled manpower, insurance is not going to help the common man. It will benefit the Insurance Companies and Private Hospitals. Many people will not be able to avail these schemes as they have no means of reaching to specialised hospitals located at a long distance from the rural area. Bearing all other costs including transportation, stay and food to the patient as well as attendant as part of the scheme for the poor may help to some extent. 

Rs. 5.00 lakh insurance for 10 crore families amounts to Rs. 50,000 crore. If we post one Doctor in each of the 2.4 lakh Gram Panchayats of the country it will cost Rs. 28,800 crore per year. Many new Hospitals can be opened every year with the balance fund of Rs. 21,200 crore. If the Government has so much of money to pay to the Private Hospitals and Insurance Companies, why not the Government thinking in direction to strengthen infrastructure and address malnutrition in rural area. Surely, this is an Election gimmick.

3500 Pradhan Mantri Jana Aushadhi Kendra is too less a number to cater to whole of India.

Out of so many schemes proposed in the manifesto only Swachh Bharat scheme is successful to some extent. But, most of the toilets constructed are not usable for poor quality of construction or for no water.

Nothing has been mentioned about population stabilisation and "National Mosquito Control Board".

Even though some success has been achieved under "Ujjwala Yojana"- it is learnt that as against that total beneficiaries of 3.3 crores, 2 crores beneficiaries were included under this scheme under other name prior to 2014. It is reported that connection are not given free by the "Distributors". Many beneficiaries are not able to refill for the next time. An impression has been created that gas and all accessories will be given free. But when the reality is realised by the beneficiary, he feels cheated. Hardly any BPL family will have money to refill the gas at more than Rs. 600/- per cylinder. It is apprehended that even those connections which are live may not be utilised by the beneficiary but, may be his employer or may be going to black market.

The initiative taken to eradicate Triple Talak is a welcome step. But the suggestions given by other Members to modify the provisions in the Bill may be agreed to so that the Act becomes effective without further delay. Many issue of the Minority have not been addressed. There is no mention of Education and job without discrimination, National Madarsa Modernisation Programme, Empower 'Waqf Board', Curate their rich heritage and culture, Preservation and promotion of Urdu, Peaceful and secure environment and Inter-faith consultative Mechanism.

Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is more of a slogan than real result at the ground level. While the Government has decided to increase maternity leave from 12 weeks to 26 weeks, many issues related to women empowerment have not been addressed. 33% reservation to women in Parliament and Assemblies has never been talked of, so also many promises in the Manifesto BJP related to women. BJP's promise to enhance wage of Anganwadi workers has been kept. The other issues of Balika Samrudhi, Ladli Laxmi, Women Health Care, strict implementation of law particularly in case of rape and Women SME in each District have not been addressed. There are increased incidence of rape and atrocities against women as there is no exemplary and expeditious punishment to the culprit.

The Government's claim of having opened 31 crore bank accounts under Jan Dhan Yojana is appreciated but, it is complained by the public that Banks are insisting for minimum balance of Rs. 5000/- otherwise, they are deducting penalty. The Government should disclose, as to how many beneficiaries have withdrawn how much money as overdraft up to Rs. 5000/- on Zero account, as promised. 

It would be useful if the data on how many beneficiaries have taken credit for how much amount is shared with the members. 

There is acute shortage of Banks and ATMs in my Parliamentary Constituency, Nabarangpur. The problem has been compounded by the shortage of manpower and short supply of cash. As against cash requirement of Rs. 150 crore per month, cash to the extent of Rs. 60 crore is made available in Nabarangpur District. Poor internet service is other reason for people's suffering. 

We have been demanding implementation of Swaminathan Commission's recommendation for last 4 years to enhance Minimum Support Price of all agricultural produces. All along our genuine demand was suppressed even though BJP, in its manifesto had committed to implement this. On the other hand, the Government has been promising since 2014 to double farmer's income by 2022. We are talking of 2018-19 budget. The growth in agriculture sector has declined to 1.9%. There does not seem to be any positive impact on its grounds through "per drop more" crop and "testing soil health". Even if it doubles by 2022 it will be less than a return a fixed deposit would have given.

Record production of food grain and vegeTable and fruits is on account of good monsoon and hard work of farmers. Government's policies do not seem to have contributed much in this direction. 

The promises of market chain, food processing units, increasing storage capacity has been going on for year after year. The reality is farmers' suicide has increased; there is distress sale of almost all items. Perishable products are thrown on the road. Provision of Rs. 11,000/- crore towards this at this point of time is too late and too little. 

Pradhanmantri Fasal Bima Yojana has benefited the Insurance Companies than the farmers. 

None of the 99 major irrigation projects lies in Odisha. Tel Integrated Project, Middle Kolab Project and Nabarangpur Irrigation Project in Nabarangpur Parliamentary Constituency of Odisha are pending with the Centre for clearance. Agriculture and forest produces are the only means of survival of the people of this area. 

Tel Integrated Project, a tributary of Mahanadi river, is not getting clearance on the plea of Mahanadi Dispute. Central Government is not showing any interest in resolving Mahandi Dispute. It is also not directing Chhattisgarh Government to stop illegal construction of barrages across Mahanadi and its tributaries within Chhattisgarh.

Online Mandi has not benefited the farmers as it is not backed by assured procurement by the Government in case the market fails to procure at MSP. There is acute problem of internet service in my Nabarangpur Parliamentary Constituency of Odisha. Therefore farmers are hardly able to take advantage of online selling. The promise of setting up 'Regional Kisan TV Channel' has not been fulfilled. 

The Government's 'Digital India' has not reached Nabarangpur Parliamentary Constituency in Odisha. As against the requirement of about 250 mobile phone towers only about 120 are working. The towers erected under LWE scheme have become defunct. There is no internet connectivity to any of the Gram Panchayats. Internet and phone service, even in Block headquarters and towns are disrupted frequently. Thus, Digital India is a distant dream for us. 

BJP in its Election Manifesto had promised allotment of fund to the extent of 6% of GDP on education. This comes to about Rs. 9.0 lakh crore per year. It is observed that allotment has been made which is hardly 0.56% of GDP.

Uniform and quality education is a dream for the common people. None of the Universities are within top 100 of the world. The worst sufferers are the poor, SCs, STs, & weaker sections of the society.

National Testing Agency is yet to take off even though promised during the last year's budget speech of Honourable Finance Minister and to conduct Single Entrance for Engineering. Before, that, the National education Policy with uniform and common syllabus across India should be adopted. It was expected that the Government would come up with new Education Policy.

There is a need to expand the scope of syllabus which should include agriculture and Skill Development as a compulsory part to ensure 100% employability of the students. 

There is not a single innovation worth world class except the innovation of 'Zero'. Independent India cannot take credit for this. Enhanced fund allotment in innovation and to involve industry in a big way is required to be world leader. 

Even though credit is claimed by the Government of hosting international sports event, we are yet to get adequate medals in Olympics compared to our population. Rs. 6.00 lakh to 1000 talented sports persons is not enough. We have to create world class infrastructure everywhere. Rural areas are lacking very badly in infrastructure. The promise of Set up 'National Youth Advisory Council', Students loan to be made simpler and affordable and Set up 'Youth Parliament" has not been fulfilled. 

Even though satisfactory progress has been made in road connection, there is a lot to be achieved in improving performance of the Railways. Safety, Punctuality, cleanliness in station and coaches, amenities at stations and coaches are not at all satisfactory. There is heavy congestion of path and inadequate wagons to meet market demand. The issue of Diamond Quadrilateral Project with High Speed Train Network (Bullet Train) and Agri Rail Network has not been addressed. 

Ganga Rejuvenation was started with a lot of fanfare. There is no mention in the speech about its progress. There is no mention of any plan for cleaning all the rivers.

Disturbance along the border is a major concern. There is no mention of 'Zero Tolerance to Terrorism, Extremism and Crime'. Nothing is mentioned in the speech how to tackle the same.

Economy suffered due to demonetisation and irrational GST rates. The promise to 'set up special courts to stop hoarding and black marketing, set up price stabilisation fund and set up Single National Agriculture Market' has not fulfilled. 

Job creation is not just about serving 'pakoda' and constructing 'pucca ghar'. In such case the definition of job has to be redefined. Thousands of post graduates, graduates and Engineers rushing for a few post of 'safaiwala' should raise some concern in the Government. We should not be so insensitive towards the youth.

The promise of bringing back black money for foreign Banks seems to have been forgotten.

The promise of "Team India: to Improve Centre - State relation, Cooperative Federalism, Sabka Saath-Sabka Vikas, Evolve model National Development driven by states, Create Regional Council of States, 'encourage cooperation among states on security, interstate disputes, remove interregional disparities and promoting tourism', Revive Inter-State Council, National Development Council and 'Involve States in Foreign trade and commerce' has been forgotten.

The promise of Integrating the Nation: "East lacking in development, East to be at par with west, Planning based on regional aspiration" and Good Governance through: "Sabka Sath Sabka Vikas, People Centric, Time bound delivery and Minimum Government maximum Governance" has not been honoured. 

Odisha's demand for special economic package has not been considered. This would have removed the East-West disparity to some extent. There are instances of the Centre directly interfering in the working of the State. Selection of Districts under Vision India-22, not resolving Mahanadi and Polavaram dispute and sending Secretary from the Centre to review works at the District level are a few examples. 

Even though FDI was promised in the areas of job creation, infrastructure etc., it has been open to almost all fields. 

There is no mention of Judicial Reform to address:

· Justice for all

· high pendency of cases

· Filling Vacancy

· Open new courts

· Reform in appointments of Judges

· Doubles judges and courts in Sub-ordinate judiciary

· National Judicial Commission for appointment in higher Judiciary 

· Lok Adalat

· Reduce cases involving Government as litigant

There does not seem to be clarity on "Simultaneous Election".

As this is the last full budget before the next "General Election" there was a need to give a report card on all the issues promised in the Manifesto of the BJP than speaking of some achievements selectively.

मैं माननीय वित्त मंत्री जी का ध्यान मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र ठाणे के अंतर्गत आने वाले गायमुख से भिवंडी बाईपास रास्ता बनाने के लिए जरूरी निधि की तरफ दिलाना चाहता हूं, जिसकी वर्तमान लागत 1,000 करोड़ रुपए है । यह बाईपास रास्ता तैयार होने से मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र में रहने वाले लोगों को एक वैकल्पिक रास्ता मिल जाएगा जिससे उन्हें यातायात जाम की समस्या से छुटकारा मिलेगा एवं समय की भी बचत होगी। अत: आप इसके लिए निधि उपलब्ध करवाने की कृपा करें ।

बजट में रेलवे पर भी खास ध्यान देते हुए माननीय रेल मंत्री जी ने 25,000 से ज्यादा फुटफॉल वाले स्टेशनों में एस्केलेटर लगाने की घोषणा बजट में की है, कई स्टेशनों और ट्रेनों में वाई-फाई और सीसीटीवी कैमरे लगाने की बात भी कही है। मैं माननीय रेल मंत्री जी से मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र के अंतर्गत आने वाले मीरा रोड एवं भायंदर स्टेशन पर भी एस्केलेटर्स लगवाने का अनुरोध करता हूं ।

माननीय रेल मंत्री जी ने महाराष्ट्र में 11,000 करोड़ रुपए की लागत से मुंबई में  90 किलोमीटर दोहरी रेल पटरी के विस्तार करने पर ध्यान दिया है एवं मुंबई लोकल के दायरे को बढ़ाने की भी बात कही है। मैं माननीय रेल मंत्री जी का ध्यान मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र ठाणे के अंतर्गत आने वाले मध्य रेलवे पर 428 करोड़ रुपए की लागत वाले दो किलोमीटर लंबे ऐरोली-कलवा लिंक के काम की तरफ आकर्षित करना चाहता हूं। इसके बारे में बजट में भी बताया गया है जिसकी घोषणा तत्कालीन रेल मंत्री श्री सुरेश प्रभु जी ने वर्ष 2015 के रेल बजट में की थी एवं 10 दिसंबर 2016 को हमारे देश के प्रधान मंत्री जी माननीय श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी द्वारा इसके भूमि पूजन का काम हो चुका है। तीन साल से अधिक का समय बीत जाने के बाद भी अभी तक काम की शुरुआत नहीं हुई है, जिसकी वजह से इतनी महत्वपूर्ण योजना कई सालों से प्रलंबित है। इस पर तुरंत ध्यान देने की जरूरत है। यह योजना पूरी होते ही ठाणे स्टेशन पर 30 प्रतिशत यात्रियों की भीड़ में कमी आएगी एवं लोगों का समय भी बचेगा।

मैं माननीय मंत्री जी का ध्यान सिडको द्वारा ठाणे वाशी मार्ग पर बोनकोडे नामक नए रेलवे स्टेशन के प्रस्ताव की तरफ भी दिलाना चाहता हूं। सिडको द्वारा बनाए गए सभी रेलवे स्टेशनों का हस्तांतरण रेलवे के पास जल्द होना चाहिए। यह मामला 20 वर्षों से प्रलम्बित है, जिस पर आप ध्यान देंगे, ऐसी मैं आशा करता हूं। साथ ही, मैं नवी मुंबई के सभी स्टेशनों पर सीसीटीवी कैमरे और ऐस्केलेटर लगाने की मांग करता हूं।

मैं माननीय रेल मंत्री जी का ध्यान मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र के अंतर्गत आनेवाले ठाणे स्टेशन परिसर में पार्किंग प्लाजा के काम की तरफ दिलाना चाहता हूं, जिसका उद्घाटन तत्कालीन रेल मंत्री श्री सुरेश प्रभु जी ने वर्ष 2016 में किया था, लेकिन इसका आधा काम ही हुआ है। मैं माननीय रेल मंत्री जी से अनुरोध करता हूं कि वे इस काम को जल्दी पूरा करवाने की कृपा करें। दूसरी महत्वपूर्ण योजना, ठाणे तथा मुलुंड के बीच मेंटल अस्पताल की जगह पर प्रस्तावित नया ठाणे स्टेशन बनाने की मंजूरी मिल चुकी है और उसकी लागत राशि भी जमा हो चुकी है परन्तु अब तक इसके जमीन हस्तांतरण की मंजूरी महाराष्ट्र सरकार से नहीं मिलने के कारण इसका काम छःवर्षों से प्रलंबित है।

मैं माननीय रेल मंत्री जी से अनुरोध करता हूं कि वे महाराष्ट्र के माननीय मुख्य मंत्री जी से इस विषय पर बात कर जल्दी ही जमीन हस्तांतरण की मंजूरी लेकर इस स्टेशन के काम को शुरू करवाने की कृपा करें।

मैं माननीय रेल मंत्री जी से मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र ठाणे नवी मुंबई एवं मीरा रोड एवं भायंदर से जुड़ी रेल परियोजनाओं पर ध्यान देते हुए ठाणे पनवेल हार्बर मार्ग पर ज्यादा लोकल सेवा शुरू करने का अनुरोध करता हूं एवं सभी स्टेशनों पर महिलाओं के लिए शौचालयों एवं विश्राम गृहों की संख्या बढ़ाने के साथ-साथ सीसीटीवी एवं ऐस्केलेटर लगवाने की कृपा करें।
